utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-32-T, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Groome: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that document 152 be placed before Mr. Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrovic, we finished yesterday with you making a few markings on that photograph. I'm going to ask you to make one other marking. I'd ask you to take the blue pen and, if you can, can you trace a line to show us the path that the -- that you saw the horse ridden by Mr. Vasiljevic take. Indicate which street he was riding down, and perhaps if you would draw an arrow to indicate which direction they were riding.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what? I'll have to draw the street over the roof because you can't see the street. May I do that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Mitrovic, let me show you another picture and see does this more clearly indicate the road that Mr. Vasiljevic was riding down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I ask that the witness be shown Prosecution document 155, and there are copies for the court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm now looking at Prosecution document 155. Are you able to see the street that you saw Mr. Vasiljevic riding the horse down?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. This is much better, and I can then draw the line from where I spotted him. May I draw?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I put an "X" where Mitar was, where I say him?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put an "X-1" to show us where he was the first moment you saw him.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but from this angle, you can't see the street properly either but this is more or less in my direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you draw an arrow to indicate the direction that he was riding.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a side street in front of this park, so it's nearer here. You can't see that. And you can see this other side street, so I put an arrow there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you more able to clearly indicate where it was you saw him fall on this exhibit as opposed to the one we showed you yesterday? Can you more clearly indicate where you saw him fall on this picture?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you to indicate that by putting "X-2." Now, before we put that on the ELMO so you can explain it to us, I'd ask you just to write your name at the bottom of the photograph on the white portion.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to point at it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, with the pointer, would you point at "X-1," indicating the first point where you saw Mr. Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "X-1." You can't see the street again from this angle, but this is this street, in this triangle here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you saw him there while you were standing in front of the Hotel Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can we have a light on, please. It's very difficult to see anything.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. Now, can we start that again. I'm sorry, I can see an arrow leading towards that triangular square. What was the arrow?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The arrow indicates the direction which you saw Mr. Vasiljevic riding on the horse; is that correct, Mr. Mitrovic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. In this direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it appears that we can see two sides of a park that is a three-sided or triangular park; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. We can see almost the whole park, but we can't see the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there's a -- on the third side of the park, there is also a street which is obscured at this point by the roofs of the building in front of it; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're telling us or you're describing the street on the third side of the park, the side of the park that we cannot see from this photograph; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that where you saw Mr. Vasiljevic for the first time riding the horse?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he riding the horse on the park, in the grassy area, or on the street?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the street, and he was very loud because the horse wouldn't obey him and that is how I heard him, because he was speaking loudly, and that is when I then called him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you show us where you marked "X-1."

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to hold the pointer for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You have to just hold it there for a moment. Now let's have "X-1" and hold the pointer steady. Is it on the grass?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. We simply cannot see the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So it's hidden by the roofs of those buildings, but it's in the grass triangle. Is there a street that runs between the grass triangle and those buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now ask you to put the pointer and hold it on "X-2," the place where you said you saw him fall off the horse.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you to take the pen and can you trace the line between "X-1" and "X-2" to indicate the path that he took from the first place you saw him until the place where you saw him fall.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had gone back a little so that I couldn't see him for a while, but I could hear him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrovic, the street that we cannot see, were you able to see whether Mr. Vasiljevic was coming down that street and was making a left onto the street that you have now indicated? Are you able to tell us that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That street goes up. It's slightly uphill. And when I saw him there, he came back, not through the grass, because there is a curb, and then turned in the direction of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he made a left at the corner of that park and proceeded directly towards the square in front of the hotel; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a little back and then to the left, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, correct me if I am wrong; the road you've drawn this long line on, that road, if I were to walk along that road, that would take me to the Rzav bridge; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to the Rzav bridge, the Drina bridge. Because this road is slightly sloped. There is a slope and there is a slight mound and then it heads towards the Drina bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are talking about the old Drina bridge; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you, if I were to go to the opposite direction, would it be true that I would be heading directly to the Rzav bridge, the bridge over the Rzav River?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the opposite direction. He must have come from that direction because this is the main street, so the bridge over the Rzav River towards the bridge over the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I were to be coming directly from Pionirska Street to the front of the hotel, I would be just travelling along that main street, the street that you have described to us as the one that he turned onto; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, from Pionirska, then the main street starts at the Rzav bridge and ends at the Drina bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to take the red pen and can you just draw an arrow to show us the road and the direction where -- to Pionirska settlement, the Mahala section of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the photograph, you can see only half of the main street; so in the opposite direction, in this direction here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So the court knows, I did bring all the pictures available of the square, I've shown them to Defence, and they are free, they're at their disposal if they wish to make use of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'd like to return to Prosecution document 152 for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are these going to be tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I was going to tender the two of them at the same time. Can we put Prosecution document 152...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd just ask you to once again show us the spot where Mr. Vasiljevic was when you saw him fall off the horse.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this is not quite accurate. It is only approximate because of the angle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to take the blue pen and put your initials, "PM," to indicate where you were when you made this observation.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've indicated you were at the edge of the awning in front of the Visegrad Hotel; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that other -- on that other photograph, I can draw a line. That other photograph is much more accurate. That is where I can draw the line and one can see where Mitar was when I spotted him and there, where I stood. Here, if I were to draw the line here, I said the first building shields it, the second does, so you can't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's return for a moment to Prosecution Exhibit 155. Prosecution document number, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can we just get our bearings on that photograph so that we know how they compare. Is the Visegrad Hotel that white building closest to the bridge?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrovic, I'd ask you to put the number 3 on the roof of the Visegrad Hotel on this diagram, or on this photograph. And perhaps if you put number 1 on the furniture store, that will help us orient ourselves.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the roof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because the diagram is so small, I'd ask you not to draw any lines, but would you please put your initials where you were when you made your observations of Mr. Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender both of those documents into evidence as Prosecution Exhibit 152-PM and 155-PM.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Domazet -- I'm sorry, Mr. Tanaskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this Exhibit 152, one can see that the photograph is not clear at all, and the witness said that he could not find his bearings there because one could not see the most important things on this photograph. And therefore, I do not think it will be particularly advisable to admit this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The trouble, Mr. Tanaskovic, is this; that we've had a lot of cross-examination based upon it. The other photograph is perhaps clearer, but nevertheless it will be of assistance. I don't understand what the basis of the objection is. The witness did have difficulty in pointing to things, but nevertheless, now that we've got it lined up with the document 155, his evidence comes into much greater clarity. What is your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness explained certain things which prevented him from being more accurate. I have a photograph of the hotel and it looks like this, and here on this photograph 152, it is completely shielded, screened off by these other buildings and you can see the hotel when a proper photograph of it is taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's a shame that you did not offer us that yesterday. You may not have had it here, but I do not understand what the basis of your objection is. If there is a better photograph, you can put it into evidence. But at the moment, we've got a witness, when you read his transcript, his evidence is meaningless. With this photograph, it has meaning. Now, what is the problem with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have this photograph of the hotel and that is a Defence Exhibit which was tendered earlier. From here, one has an excellent view of the hotel and the area in front of the hotel. And the photograph which is Prosecution Exhibit 152, that photograph is taken from an angle from which the witness cannot establish exactly the place, cannot locate exactly the place where the accused fell. The other photograph is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I wish you had brought it to our attention yesterday, that's all. But I still don't understand the basis of your objection. It will be Exhibit P152. Now, have you got any objection to 155?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. The next one will be P155. Now, Mr. Groome, that you've had your attention drawn to this Defence exhibit, do you want to use it in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm actually planning to introduce it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask now that the witness be shown Prosecution document number 17-11. I'm sorry, Your Honour, this actually is in evidence already; it's Prosecution Exhibit 17-11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It was introduced on the 17th of September, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrovic, I would ask you to take a look at Prosecution Exhibit 17-11. Do you recognise what's depicted in that photograph? I'd ask you not to make any marks until I ask you to, please.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see the Visegrad Hotel and the exact spot where I was. Now, if this photograph were put together with your 155, then - this is what, 17 or 7? - and if we put together those photographs, then it will be quite clear. I -- the first photograph was also clear to me, but it was very difficult for me to explain it to you. Of course I was quite clear about it because that is where I live, that is where I spend my time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrovic, I'd ask you to make two markings on this exhibit. First, would you please just write your name at the bottom of the exhibit so we know that it's you that's making the markings.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd ask you also to draw a circle on the spot of ground where your feet were when you were -- you made your observations of Mr. Vasiljevic. Indicate the spot on the ground where you were standing and put your initials inside it.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a small place so I made a mistake, but can I put my initials underneath?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I hear you what you're saying, you're saying that you made a mistake. I'd ask you to draw an "X" through your mistake and draw a circle to indicate the spot where you were standing.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the circle is all right, but it's very small so I can't put my initials in it. Can I put them underneath?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that would be fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask now that that be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrovic, I'd ask if you would take the pointer and hold it at where you were standing.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And am I correct in describing where you have indicated as the very edge of a walkway underneath the awning; is that correct? I need you to answer verbally for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you are quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this particular copy of 17-11 as 17-11-PM.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection to that, Mr. Tanaskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Exhibit P17-11-PM.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mitrovic, can you give us an idea, what speed was this horse travelling when you saw it travel from this triangular-shaped park to the place where it fell? How fast was Mr. Vasiljevic going?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slow. He was going very slowly and the horse was not moving in a straight line because it was refusing to obey so that his hind legs were moving -- I don't know how to explain it -- and he was striking it with that rope. So he was moving slowly. It was raining and I don't really know about what it happens when you put horseshoes, I don't know whether he had them or not, so that -- but it was moving very slowly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you recognised this horse as a Bosnian mountain horse; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, drawing on the logic from the school, that was at a time when I was still very young, but I remembered, yes, that that should be the Bosnian mountain horse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for those of us not familiar with the terrain of Bosnia, Bosnia in many places is very mountainous and is made up of very many steep slopes; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And many of those slopes are rocky slopes; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. If it's a road, then it's not rock, it's macadam or something like that, mixed with earth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you would agree with me that most mountains and hills in Bosnia are far steeper than the incline in the square, would you not?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now yesterday during your testimony, if I'm not mistaken, you never told us when you saw this, and my question to you this morning is: When was the first time that you were asked to give a date regarding when you made this observation? When was the first time you were asked to give a date, if you ever were?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked that when I was giving my statement to lawyer Tanaskovic and I didn't know the date and that is why I said approximately June up to the middle of July; I could not remember the exact date. And that is why, in my statement, there is no date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in your statement, you did say that it occurred on a Serb religious holiday; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I come from Montenegro so that I don't know much about these holidays. I was told that later on, but I simply don't know about that. Somebody told me that, but I don't know about that and I did not pay any attention, nor did I know that that was a special date until I started making my statement, and in my statement, I said I did not know. So I gave a rather broad answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that somebody told you about that; told you about what?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was this conversation about when that had happened, in my school and other places, and then some other people said that Visegrad Serbs are very religious people, that they were serious believers and that those holidays served them as landmarks, as benchmarks, whereas I am an atheist so I don't know that, and they told me that, yes, they could base their reckoning, their recollections on those holidays.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were any of those people that you're referring to, any of those people witnesses in this case?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Witness Ratko or Ratomir Simsic, and we talked about it before we came here and we talked about this and I told him too, I know nothing about religious holidays, so that I don't know. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what you did say to us here today is that it happened sometime, I believe you said from the middle of June up until possibly the middle of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From the beginning of June up to the middle of the month, but that is my personal opinion. You know, when we start talking about something, then we cannot always agree. Not only in Visegrad because everybody has, of course, his -- has his own angle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrovic, I want to just read you from the transcript just a few moments ago just to be clear on this issue. In response to one of my questions, you said, "I was asked that when I was giving my statement to lawyer Tanaskovic and I didn't know the date and that is why I said approximately June up to the middle of July. I could not remember the exact date and that is why, in my statement, there is no date." Did you say just a few minutes ago that it could have occurred up until the middle of July?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Beginning of June up to the middle of June, it could have been interpreter's mistake. In July, I was assigned to a completely different place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mitrovic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Groome, but maybe I've misunderstood that answer. Oh, I see. You had asked him whether it could have occurred up to the middle of July and he said no, only until June. I'm sorry. Yes, any re-examination, Mr. Tanaskovic? Re-examined by Mr. Tanaskovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When Mr. Groome asked him, the witness said that in July 1992, he was elsewhere, not where he was before that. My only question is: Where was he? So I'm talking now about July 1992; where were you in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In July 1992, I was west of Visegrad, assigned to a school. We provided -- we were guarding Visegrad from an attack from the west and the road. The only exit towards Sarajevo, Pale, or Rogatica, and that was macadam -- no, it wasn't, but it was a rather bad road which went via Rogatica, then Semec, Borika, Rogatica, and so on. And those who took that road, that is, if somebody took that road, then one had to go to take an APC, that is, one needed escort because that road was not safe there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that means that you were not in Visegrad in July at all?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, now I'd like the witness to be shown the proposed Exhibit 155, to draw that line which he already drew on the Exhibit 152, because this photograph is much clearer, and to show us where he was in front of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Tanaskovic, he has already drawn a line on Exhibit 155, showing the path that your client took.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I was suggesting, Your Honour, was a line from the spot where the witness showed he was standing to the spot where he saw Mitar Vasiljevic fall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, we better do that with a different coloured pen. We've got red and blue on it now; have you got another colour? A green one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you repeat what you want me to draw?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the spot where you were standing in front of the hotel to the spot where you marked that Mr. Vasiljevic fell. And also that "X" on the roof of the building, that is the line showing where you saw Vasiljevic for the first time and where you were standing.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there's the angle obstructing the view of the Sipad store, it's very close by. Do you have a ruler or something? Then it's quite visible. If I don't need a ruler, then it will be an approximate line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead, yes, draw the line.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph is a bit confusing too. You want me to do it in green?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, in green.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph is also confusing, you see, because I have to go to the left. Here it is, roughly. The marker is not very good so you can't see the line very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show that to us now, indicate?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was standing here, and I saw Vasiljevic in this direction here, and then he turned back a bit, turned to the left, and was moving in this direction, and then Simsic called out to him. He turned around, and that's where he fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark on this photograph the building or, rather, can you tell us whether the house in which Simsic lives can be seen on this photograph, if you know.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see it. It's just the tiny part of it, a balcony, so I can mark it with an "X-3" if you like. I'm sorry, this marker is no good, can I use the black one? No, you can't see the balcony. That is it. "X-3."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So "X-3" is the balcony of Mr. Simsic's house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I should like to tender this photograph now, with the added markings, as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It already is an exhibit. The one that he's actually marked is P155/PM.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to suggest that the additional markings be included. Your Honour, I have no further objections, but I would suggest, while the witness is still here, earlier on, a tape was tendered into evidence with this part of Visegrad, the Pionirska Street, by the Prosecution. I think it was tendered on the 9th of October. The number is 332, from 2125 to 2208 minutes, so it's not long. So it shows this part of the town we've been talking about so I think it would be a good idea for us to show it to the witness for him to be able to indicate on that video clip the things he has been telling us about now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: First of all, I do not understand what you are saying about the photograph. The photograph, which is in evidence, has in fact been marked by the witness. So the markings that he has made, the most recent ones at your request, are part of the exhibit. It doesn't have to be re-tendered in order to get those markings into evidence. So I'm afraid I don't understand what you mean when you are re-tendering it. The next thing is, have you given the booth any warning that you wanted this tape played?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm afraid not. But we thought it would be necessary because this witness can make things very much clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you had thought --

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the benefit of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you wanted this played, you should have given somebody a warning about it. These things can't be pulled out of the air. Now, could someone help us with what the exhibit number really is?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number 18, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: 18, right. Can we have the tape please, Exhibit 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a copy with us as well, if necessary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is it cued at 2125? These things take time, Mr. Tanaskovic. You really have to assist us better than this. Now, we wanted to cue it at 2125 and it's to play to 2208. Well, we'll have to play it from the beginning because the reference 2125 doesn't appear on any counter that we have in the booth. How far in is it, Mr. Tanaskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's about 20 minutes into the tape, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And your copy of it is not cued to start at the right place either; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm afraid not. We were viewing it last night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think we'll have to bring this witness back later when it can be lined up, but next time you want anything like this done, you must have it ready. You must warn either the Prosecution or the court deputy to have the thing ready and cued at the right place. We simply don't have time to waste 20 minutes, waiting here for it to come up. So, sir, I'm afraid you will have to wait --

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. May I say straight away that the next witness is Simsic, so we will need the tape again for him and thank you very much for telling us what we should do, but I wish to notify you in advance that we will need the tape for him too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: With some prescience, the booth operator believes he might have it at the right spot, so he's going to play it to see if he has it at the right spot and you can show it so this witness. Let's have a go.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's it. It's quite right, exactly that.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly the place where I saw Mitar. You can see it clearly. If you could wind it back a bit and then stop. Can I show you anything; can I point to places?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It would be impossible for to you point to places, I'm afraid, sir. Now, is that all you wanted to show or do you want more of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the part of the park where the witness saw Mr. Vasiljevic, and you can see the street going towards the hotel, precisely what the witness couldn't show you a moment ago to show you where he spotted him the first time and where exactly he was standing in front of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we were to rewind the tape a little, then I could explain to you the park and the street, which cannot be seen on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Then we'll stop it and rewind it just a little bit to where we started the last time, and we're very grateful to the audio visual people for being able to assist us. Now, may I suggest you let the witness describe it this time because he's the one giving the evidence, not you, Mr. Tanaskovic, so he can describe it to us as the film is being played.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that's what I had in mind, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as I see the spot, can I ask them to stop, to stop the tape, and then it will be clearer for you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You certainly can. [Videotape played].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop it there, please. This is the street to the left, going uphill. Behind the car is the park, and that is the street you can't see on the photograph. Please go on with the tape.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you stop there, please. Just behind this car is the house of Zoran Stancic, the Beko store should be there, a clothing store, and he was moving in this direction and that was the line I drew from the hotel behind this car. Please play on.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then he turned back, you see, where this car is, next to the traffic sign we just saw, and headed along the main street. Now, you can see the hotel. Could you stop there, please. A little back. A little backward, please. That's why I was saying that this building in front of the hotel on those photographs, you can see the awning of the hotel here. Across the middle of the photograph where the bench is, behind the bench, and there you can see the Sipad store on the corner, and there is the balcony also. You can see the balcony where the teacher Simsic lives. I think it's the second balcony on the top floor. Please play on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Wait a minute. The place you were standing at the hotel, is that at the very left of the picture at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You can see a flower bed in front of the hotel that I showed you, and this is the direction which goes across the spot where the bench is and also the shop I showed a moment ago. I heard the noise and the treading of the horse, and I turned around and, as there was no one in the street, I turned around and called him and he came immediately somewhere where the car is, in front of the hotel. That's where he fell. And Ratko saw him when he passed by his balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what we wanted to show Your Honour. Thank you, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We better keep the tape for the next witness too. Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just one question arising out of that video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Re-cross-examined by Mr. Groome:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrovic, what you're referring to as a park now, we see it in the video tape, back in let's say March of 1992, that wasn't a park, was it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was a mosque there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was a mosque; correct? Now, for you to have been able to see the things that you're telling us you saw, that mosque would have had to have been knocked down; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I didn't see who knocked it down or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it knocked down? When was it knocked down?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know it was destroyed, but I can't remember the date. Whether it was in May or not, I don't know. I know it was in that time period, but I don't know exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I'm clear about the question you asked. Are you suggesting that there was a mosque there at the time the witness says he saw the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I think what the witness has just said is that there was a mosque there in March and sometime in May, sometime before he made his observations, that mosque was knocked down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I see. Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment. You will get a chance to re-examine in a moment. Judge Taya is going to ask a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. Thank you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TAYA
utterances.text: You said you were not in Visegrad in July 1992. When you left Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TAYA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was deployed, I think it was Donja Lijeska, three or four kilometres by road, so to the west of Visegrad, across the Drina bridge and up the hill, behind the hotel, the other bank of the river, the left bank of the river.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TAYA
utterances.text: Yes, but my question is when you left Visegrad, where you were in the latter part of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand correctly, my unit, the one I described yesterday, when it was assigned to the hotel after being given assignments to ensure security at the entrance, we were transferred three or four kilometres back to secure the road, the Visegrad-Rogatica road, so that was our assignment. We covered the area from Visegrad to Donja Lijeska, then there was the Rogatica unit and we were linked up so as to be able to reach Pale and the other places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TAYA
utterances.text: Were you in Visegrad until the end of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think, if I may suggest, the question is more directed to when was it that you were transferred or assigned away from the hotel? Can you give us a date in June or July when it was you were last at the hotel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact date. I don't know. I don't remember. We didn't stay at the hotel long, so after the 20th, the 25th or around the 1st, I just can't remember. But I know that we stayed at the hotel briefly. I don't even know exactly for how many days, I didn't pay attention. I was scared for my own life, so the dates didn't really interest me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tanaskovic, you can re-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Further examined by Mr. Tanaskovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would just like the witness to tell us, when he was telling us where he saw Mr. Vasiljevic from, had the mosque already been destroyed when he saw Vasiljevic or not?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it had been destroyed. The Prosecutor asked me and I confirmed that the mosque had been destroyed. Had there been a mosque there, then only a magician would be able to see through the mosque walls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean, Mr. Mitrovic, that there was a park or something like the park there?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly when the park was laid out, but the mosque was destroyed. Whether there were just the ruins or the park at the time, I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I should have asked you, Mr. Groome, did you want to ask anything out of Judge Taya's or my questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you for coming along to give evidence and for the evidence you have given. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you please make the solemn declaration in the document which the court usher is showing you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Tanaskovic. Examined by Mr. Tanaskovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Simsic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us -- I shall begin by asking you to give us your full name and the place and date of your birth.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: My name is Ratomir Simsic. I was born on the 1st of October, 1942 in the village of Stanisevac municipality of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, do you have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I do have a nickname. I have had it since practically the day of my birth. I am Ratko or Rale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are Ratomir Simsic, called Ratko or Rale; is that it?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us something about your education and what you do.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I completed the teacher's academy and then I -- teacher's vocational school and then I was an exemplary student at the teacher's academy, so that I am a teacher by profession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where did you work?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I worked all over. Do you want me to give you all those places?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I spent most of my career in Visegrad and its environs. For two years, I worked in Croatia, in different schools.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what are you doing now?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Well, for the past 22 months, I have been a pensioner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when is it that you moved to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I've lived in Visegrad for a long time; since February 1974.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in June or in 1992 as such, but especially in June, where is it that you lived in Visegrad? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I lived on the main street, Marsala Tita 38. The number, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what it was called then?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Now it is called King Peter I, number 38 again. I mean, it's the same flat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe with some detail the building where your flat is.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course I can because I have lived in that building de jure and de facto for the past 15 or 16 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe it then, to us.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean the site. Where the building is.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Oh, I see. The building is in the very heart of the town, on the square, and it is called the corner building, uga onica. There are three entrances. It is a three-storeyed building, that is, it has two floors, a few flights, not -- downstairs there are some shops next to it and in front of it is the Sipad furniture store. To the left is a grill restaurant and the department store, and to the right is the Visegrad Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that downstairs you have some shops?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What shop was it before the war and what is it now?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Before the war, it was Jugoplastika and now it's Petrofar right below my apartment even though there are some other shops there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, do you know Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. I know him very well indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, how is it that you came to know him and where?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Well, I've known him for the past 20 years at least and I know him as a waiter who worked in a number of outlets, in a hotel, different restaurants and other hotels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that you mention those restaurants and hotels, can you tell us which company to all they belong to?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: They belonged to UTP Panos, in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the war, did you have any assignment either as a military man or under labour duty in Visegrad or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Why, yes. I don't know how to put it because I'm an invalid, but I did have an assignment, yes. I was assigned to the bus terminal, Visegradtrans, Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time frame, and I mean 1992 or, more specifically, the middle of that year, that is mid-1992, did you used to see Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic around?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I saw him in the former half of June 1992 as a kind of a monitor, as a man who was responsible for the cleanliness of the town, a duty officer in the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "monitor, man responsible for the cleaning of the town," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Well, in my personal view - and I make this reservation - he was engaged in the drive to clean the town of broken glass, all sorts of election posters, leaves, branches; that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that the town was pretty unkempt, pretty neglected in that regard?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you used to see Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic as a monitor around, could you see what he was doing and who else was doing it with him?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I did. Well, as I said, they were collecting and removing this broken glass and old posters and fallen leaves and other refuse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question had to do more with who else participated in that? Did you see anyone doing that?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did. Every saleswoman worked in front of her shop. That is, none of them was exempt from that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when you saw Mr. Vasiljevic clean and organise the cleaning of streets, can you remember how he was dressed, at least on one occasion?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. He wore a kind of a dark suit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he, perhaps, have any weapon on him?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a hat?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember if Mr. Vasiljevic, at the time when you saw him in those dark clothes, as you say, did he wear anything else?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: He had a red armband on his left arm. It was about five, six centimetres wide, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see or could you see if on this armband which was red, as you say, was there an emblem, a sign of something, a symbol?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Absolutely none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means red, just plain red?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Just plain red.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, until when did you used to see Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic do what you told us?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Right up to the -- to Sunday, which was the 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Same year, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened that 14th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: On the 14th of June, 1992, it was a religious holiday, the Holy Trinity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I know, the orthodox call it the Holy Trinity or the first Trinity.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I said it is the first Trinity or the Holy Trinity because there are three Trinities; Monday, Tuesday, the second and the third.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, on the 14th, it was the first Holy Trinity, on the 15th, it was the second, and on the 16th, it was the third?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago, I asked you what happened on that 14th of June, 1992, because you said you used to see him until that date. Now, what is it that happened on that 14th of June?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Well, I've just told you, it was the first Trinity, which is a major Christian religious holiday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Simsic, I am asking you in relation to Mr. Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Oh, I see. May I ask you a question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, you may not.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you on that 14th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: On the 14th of June, 1992 I was at home, or better said, in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean that flat which you described in the beginning of your testimony, is it?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the flat where I lived then and where I live now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happened? You were at home.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was at home in the flat and I was sitting and reading newspapers, watching television, and my son, the youngest one, had just run into the kitchen from the room and said to me, and I quote, "Daddy, please come and look at this wonder." "Oh, come on, son, what is there to see?" Because there was nothing nice to see, it was all very monotonous. But I went out onto the balcony, and I saw Mr. Mitar on a horse, riding down the street towards the hotel, the Visegrad Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that moment, when you came out onto the balcony and saw him, where was he in relation to your balcony?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: He was halfway between the balcony and the place where the event or the accident took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your son who had called you out onto the balcony to see that wonder, what is his name?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I think I said it, but perhaps I didn't. His name is Bojan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, how old was he?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: He was 12, about 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Tanaskovic, remember to pause before you ask the question. You are coming in over the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what direction was Mr. Vasiljevic moving, riding that horse?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Well, I've said it; he was moving down the street because there is a slight inclination, a slight slope, and he was moving towards the Visegrad Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us what happened next?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Well, I can say that it was raining at the time, that it was late afternoon, at about dusk, but the visibility was still good, and I cried out, "Good for you, Mitar." At about the same time, Mitar fell off the horse, and the horse fell over Mitar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which means that the horse was over Mr. Vasiljevic, pressing him down?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. His whole body was on him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear, as you were watching it from your balcony, did you hear Mitar Vasiljevic cry out, scream, moan; anything?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. He was crying out for help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did anyone go to him?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes, somebody did but I don't know who. And all I heard was his words, "Don't touch me. If you can, get the ambulance."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you cannot remember who is it that went to him to help him?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: No, but I guess -- I suppose it was somebody from the Visegrad Hotel because it is only 50 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you then go on watching that event from your balcony?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: No, because I was very sorry, I simply cannot bear to watch anyone suffering.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what happened then to Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Well, I do. I was told that by others, that in a very short while, after a very short delay, somebody from the health centre arrived in an ambulance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you were on the balcony, could you see what happened to the horse whom Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic had been riding?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The horse just leapt up like a doe, it moved over to the other side onto the pavement and stood there, and after the transport, that is, other people told me that he seemed to be petrified there, rooted to the pavement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Simsic, if you can remember, will you please tell us what colour, if you happened to notice or if you remember, what colour was the horse that Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic had been riding?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It was black or grey; dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we -- and in terms of height or the size, what would you say, what horse was that, from that point of view?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I remember it very well; it was an ordinary horse, small, mountain horse, dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time when you saw Mr. Vasiljevic riding, do you remember what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I said that a long time ago. I said that he had a grey suit on, a dark suit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you saw Mr. Vasiljevic riding, you say it was raining. Did Mr. Vasiljevic have a raincoat, a hat, or some other clothes of that type, an overcoat?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Well, the rain came in waves, but he did not have either an overcoat or a hat or anything. He was just wearing that suit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him riding, did you see something else on him, something out of the ordinary, something that would draw your attention, or not?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Well, I said I saw that red ribbon on the left arm, and otherwise, nothing in particular. A red armband, red colour, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Simsic, you -- this is the first time you said, because you said earlier that you saw him wearing it at the time when he was cleaning the streets, that's why I asked you.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see him have something in his hands, or rather, when he fell, did you see whether there were any other objects there on the scene?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: In his right hand, he held a rather long, a rather thick rope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he do with that rope?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: He was trying to egg the horse on, striking the horse to speed it up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you saw that, how fast or how slow was the horse moving?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Well, neither too fast nor too slow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It would be an appropriate time, Mr. Tanaskovic. We'll adjourn now until 11.30.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tanaskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Simsic, let us continue where we broke off at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you a moment ago whether you noticed, when you saw Mitar Vasiljevic on horseback, any objects on him and you said, except for the rope, you hadn't noticed anything. I would like to know when this happened on the asphalt road, did you see anything else next to the horse, or nothing, did you see nothing?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. I didn't see --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't see anything else?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what a megaphone or loudspeaker is?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, perhaps, notice on Vasiljevic such a loudspeaker after he fell?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: No, not at all. I did not. Nothing like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we were describing a moment ago the horse that Mr. Vasiljevic was riding, I omitted to ask you whether the horse had a saddle or a wooden saddle that we call samar or a normal, leather saddle?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: You don't need to explain to me what is a samar and what is a sedlu because I am -- come from the villages. No, he didn't have anything. He was riding bareback. The horse didn't have a saddle or a pack saddle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your testimony, you told us what time of day it was when this incident or accident happened, as you described it. Could you tell us roughly about what time it could have been?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said it was afternoon, before dusk, so it was between 4.00 and 5.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you left the balcony, that you went inside and didn't continue watching. Did you hear afterwards or learn in one way or another what happened to Mr. Vasiljevic after that, or rather, did he suffer any injuries as a result of this?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I've told you that too. I said that I learnt from others very shortly after the event because I couldn't watch his suffering because I, too, long ago in 1974 broke a leg and I know what it means and it's very painful. At least, it was for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what did you learn about his injuries?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I learned that he broke his leg. I didn't know which, but I later learnt about that. I thought that he had broken his back too, but I was sure that he must have had a broken leg or arm or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear or learn where he was treated for his injuries?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I heard and I can claim that he was treated at the General Hospital in Uzice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this event, at some time later, did you see Mr. Vasiljevic again?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did because I had been advised by doctors to walk a lot because of my condition, so I walk down the Drina towards Vojvode Stepe Street, where his house is, and further on, towards the Vilina Vlas motel, and I saw him on crutches that same year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean in front of his house?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes, as I said, in Vojvode Stepe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Let us go back to the Sunday of the 14th of June, 1992. Can you tell us now on the basis of what are you claiming and remembering that it was the 14th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I can because I'm saying for the third time, I'm telling you about this religious custom. It always falls in June, this Trinity, and the first day of the Trinity is always observed on a Sunday and I remember well that that was the date because on the third of the Trinity, the 16th, on a Tuesday in 1992, as my Slava is St. John The Baptist, that is my patron saint's day, I didn't have an icon, I had to take it to the church to be seen by Father Rajko, the priest, with his signature and his stamp on the back of the icon, indicating that the icon had been blessed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you had the icon blessed, is that a custom among the Serbs or is it up to each individual to decide what to do?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: That's a good question because it was a sin to celebrate without an icon and an oil lamp, but if you couldn't purchase one, God would forgive you. But as I had purchased one, Father Rajko advised me to leave it in the church for a couple of hours for him to bless it, and for me this was a special experience because I know now that I am celebrating my patron saint's day the way it should be celebrated, properly. So it is a custom, in answer to your question, and that is how it should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mentioned Father Rajko just now, who did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I was referring to one of three priests who were working in that church. Of course, I wasn't referring to my father, because I don't even remember him, I was too small. What I meant was the priest Rajko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the priest who did this, his name is Rajko; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: His name is Rajko -- oh, please, help me with the surname. Ceticomin [phoen] -- Cvjetkovic, I'm sorry, if it's important, Cvjetkovic, Rajko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To clarify the word "bless," or "consecrate," can we call it a kind of blessing?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, because as I was saying, one couldn't celebrate your patron saint's day properly. Better to celebrate it in one way or another, but the most important symbols are this icon and the oil lamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Let us move on to another area. A moment ago, you were telling us that you were watching the event from your balcony. Could you now describe in your own words the spot where you saw Mr. Vasiljevic fall off his horse and how the horse fell at the same time.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I told you a moment ago, but I can repeat it. This happened on the right-hand side of the carriageway on the square, the side closer to my building and the Sipad furniture store. And if you are looking down the street, then you have the catering establishment grill and the department store; and further forward, on the right-hand side, is the Visegrad Hotel. In relation to my balcony, I said it was halfway between my balcony and the place of the accident. So viewed from the balcony, it was some 20 or 30 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I asked you this, you were telling us that Mr. Vasiljevic was moving towards the hotel, so to his right was your balcony, the furniture store, and to the left was the grill restaurant. Who owned it?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: It belonged to the catering and tourist enterprise Bosna, that's what it used to be. Now it is the TP Visegrad that is the owner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes, and further on, on the left-hand side, is the department store. On the right-hand side is my building, the Sipad furniture store and, further on, the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Wait. Just wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In front of this furniture store, Sipad that you called it?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Sipad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a parking lot or something like that, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is to the left of that parking space?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: To the left of the parking space, as I was saying, is the grill belonging to the commercial enterprise Visegrad, and in front of the grill is a tiny mini-park and at the end of that park, towards the hotel, is a billboard with notices about films showing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to all these landmarks that you mentioned, where would you place the spot of the fall? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: The spot of the fall is on the right-hand side of the road facing the hotel because there is a path for unloading large lorries with furniture and that is also their parking space belonging to the furniture shop. That's as much as I can say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be prepared to identify your building and your balcony from which you were watching what you've just told us about?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Of course I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask Your Honours for this short video clip to be shown to this witness for the witness to identify his building, if he can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Starting from the same spot, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the same spot is possible, but he's just talking about his own balcony and his own building. Maybe we can just show him his building, that's a bit later on than the place where we started showing the tape a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think it would be simpler for the booth to start from the same position.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There it is. Could you stop that? Could you stop there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Would you stop it and wind it back just slightly, thanks. If you could wind it back. Now stop. Is that where you wanted it, Mr. Tanaskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Simsic, do you recognise on this shot any of the places that you described today?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I like this shot very much. It's an excellent shot. I can see my balcony here, I can see another building that I didn't mention - I don't think it's important; the old hotel - and the new hotel, you can't see it very well, it's further forward. You can't see the grill or the department store, but I don't think that's so important. You can almost see the actual spot where this happened. You can't see the pedestrian crossing and the carriageway completely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Simsic, will you please show us which is the balcony you were telling us about today.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: How can I show it to you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, explain. You can see the building, you can see balconies; explain it.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Well, I am in the building with the green facade, or rather, next to it, and it's the second balcony beneath the roof. Out of these four balconies, there's the first and then the second, and that is where Jugoplastika used to be, and above it is my balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it's on the top floor, the second in line. I think that is clear now. I think, for the record, the witness has indicated the balcony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you want the video any longer?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Ossogo:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ratomir Simsic, I am trial attorney for the Prosecution and we will dwell for a few minutes on the testimony you have given regarding the events you eye witnessed on the Marsala Street, number 38. First of all, could you give us more precision regarding your relationship with Mr. Mitar that you said you knew very well. I would like to ask you for how long you have known Mr. Mitar. Could you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: What I said once I am not denying. I have known him for some 20 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew him as a neighbour or as a friend? Did you become friends or did you have any other particular kind of relationship?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: As a friend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you saw him often during the war and before. Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I would see him mostly while he was working at the hotel, at his workplace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never visited him at home?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he never visited you at home?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How frequently would you meet, shall we say per week or per month, over a period of 20 years?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Occasionally, and by chance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his wife, possibly?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did know her extremely well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the other members of his family?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I know his daughter who went to school with my son Bojan - they are the same generation, the son I just mentioned - and I know his father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from his daughter, do you know what other children he had?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I know he also had a son called Nikola. He was younger than his sister. I think his name was Nikola. Nikola and Nikolina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are going to dwell for a moment on the places where the events that we are discussing occurred. You said that you were living in Marsala Street until the month of May 1993, if I'm not mistaken. When did you move there, or rather, how long have you been living in the apartment that has just been shown you on the video clip?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: I moved to that apartment on the 16th of June, 1986. That is when I was given this small, one-room apartment by my school. Then I left that apartment in 1993 and then went back to that same apartment exactly on the 9th of November, 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you claim that you really know that area, the neighbourhood of that house, all around it?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: You mean on the photograph, on the video?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but in the first place, I mean that area, that is, the streets, the houses, the shops there, the geographic area, the one in which you live.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR SIMSIC
utterances.text: Very well, indeed. I know it and I watched the scene of the incident as if in the palm of my hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you shared your flat, Mr. Simsic, with whom?
