utterances.text: Mr. Tanaskovic, he has said twice that the general procedure was to get an x-ray. He assumed that's where the accused was taken. How can he tell us what was in the x-ray? That's, if I may say so, an outrageous attempt to get in a pure guesswork. I would be more interested to know where the documents are that told him where to go and what time it was the call was received and everything myself. Are you going to ask him about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wanted to see if the witness knew, or rather, if he saw that x-ray. That is why I asked him that and I don't want to ask him anything more about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, you were there, you were present in the health centre, that is what you told us at the beginning. And after this procedure was finished, did somebody take Mr. Vasiljevic to Uzice?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: I took him there. I took him there in the ambulance car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any papers, any documentation for that travel?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he had the doctor's referral, the diagnosis, and with that, he was going to Uzice and it would also show, it would also indicate which ward he was to go to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you left for Uzice, was medical aid extended to him and what kind of?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that. There are doctors, there are nurses, I really don't know anything about it. They merely tell me that the patient is ready, I put them in the car. Now, whether anything was administered to him, I mean doctors know these things. I never go into that. I am merely given the referral or they give it to the patient so he can look after it because I have to drive the car and mind the car, so the patient keeps the referral papers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if you or Mr. Vasiljevic carried that documentation, I mean the x-rays of his leg?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is the usual procedure. Every patient is given that, that both the x-rays and the referral, and then the patient takes those along so that he does not have to go through another x-ray. Even now, I mean, when I have to do the same thing, then I give it usually to the patient. Or if somebody is escorting that patient, a relative or somebody, I give it to them for fear that I might lose those papers and that is how it's always been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that it was practice or predominantly. Now, my question is did you or did you not; do you know or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: I had the referral and that travel order on the basis of which a car can go somewhere, and the referral is given to the patient to take it with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And secondly, do you know or do you remember or have you forgotten if Mr. Vasiljevic had those x-rays in the car with him?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't tell you now because it is mostly nurses and those personnel there get all this ready and put it in the ambulance car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you leave the health centre to go to Uzice, at about what time?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: I think it must have been close to 1900.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you and Mr. Vasiljevic alone in that vehicle or was somebody else with you?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: Miloje Novakovic is a man who also works in the health centre and he asked if he could also come along if there was any case to be taken to Uzice because he was to undergo a medical check-up there at a doctor, so he asked if he could come along, and for safety, too, for safety reasons as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So because of safety?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: Well, you know, sometimes we would be told, you know, the road is not safe. Sometimes there is some gunfire and all the passengers get off and try to hide and they don't feel safe and so you have to wait until it's safe again to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on your way from Visegrad to Uzice, did you stop anywhere?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I stopped in Vardiste at the uncle's because Mitar told me, "Drop by my uncle." His uncle is his mother's brother. So we stopped there - that man is a publican - he asked for a blanket. I presume he was cold and then the -- and she then brought him a fruit juice or something and we were there for a short while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long, could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think it could not have been less than 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that road, were there any checkpoints or -- and which?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were two of them but then I showed them their referrals, they see what it's about, and there were two such crossings and that is where we were delayed also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you arrive in Uzice?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: I arrived there, it could have been about 40 minutes past 8.00. At 20 to 9.00, that's when I arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do then with Mr. Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: Well, the procedure is when I bring a patient to Uzice, then there is a doctor on duty in the reception surgery, and there are also nurses and they then take the patient over and took him to another x-ray. And I have to wait there until I'm told the patient is admitted. And they have their special service who do that and they called Aleksandar Moljevic, the doctor responsible for the orthopaedic ward, and he looked at the x-rays and he said take him to me, I believe it's on the fourth floor, the patient was taken there then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have to sign anything that you are handing over the patient, or rather, that you left the patient in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, at that time nobody had to sign it. No, no, I did not have to sign anything because there was only the referral on the basis of which he was admitted and that referral stays with the hospital and that is how they draw up the invoice and then charge for the treatment because Uzice is in Serbia and Visegrad is in Bosnia and that referral was used to then charge the insurance service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, you told us that he was admitted to the hospital by the ward doctor, Dr. Moljevic. In large hospitals, as far as I know, I don't know if you will agree with me, there is the doctor, the doctor on duty for the hospital as a whole. Was there any such doctor or not?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the reception department, you have a doctor on duty, but otherwise, every individual ward has its own doctors on duty, depending. I mean, surgeries, surgical wards, the orthopaedic wards will have the doctor on duty and that is where the patient is then referred to and examined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of that doctor? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The translation has just stopped. You've just -- you must give them more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that doctor who was on duty in the general reception room; do you know who that is? Do you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: I don't. I would recognise him if I saw him. And recently somebody told me that he was retired. I asked the other day somebody and I asked about -- somebody else asked about that particular doctor and he said he's been pensioned off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From all that you have told us, it transpires that in the Uzice hospital, they again made another x-ray of Vasiljevic's leg?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your testimony, you said that Mr. Novakovic came along with you, was in the car with you. Was he all the time with you or what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: He also returned with me. He went to the hospital. Where in the hospital precisely, I don't know. He had to have a check-up. Something was wrong with his sight or I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of all that, in your view, how long did you stay at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: About 45 minutes. It is when they tell me that the patient has been admitted that I can go back, so I may have spent in Uzice another half hour or so to buy something, to do some chore or the other and then I went back. I think I returned about 2300.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell us, did you often go to the Uzice hospital because you were a driver?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: I did, because there was no other hospital to take patients to except Uzice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, when you left Vasiljevic behind in the hospital, after that, did you go there?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: Of course I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, did you ever visit Mr. Vasiljevic, go to see Mr. Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: ZIVORAD SAVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. My sister worked in Uzice, she was a cook and she distributed food among the wards and she reported to me about patients and I also went to see them. Whenever I had time, I'd go and see people who came from Visegrad, who were from Visegrad like I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's a convenient time, Mr. Tanaskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now and resume at 9.30 in the morning.
